key_insight: SpecEyes parallelizes the agentic loop by speculatively predicting future percepts and plans so the multimodal LLM can execute ahead of completed visual-tool calls, drastically reducing sequential overhead (agentic depth).
problem_solved: Agentic MLLMs suffer high latency and poor system concurrency because repeated perception→reasoning→tool-call cycles force strictly sequential processing (large agentic depth).
method: Speculative perception: lightweight predictors generate anticipated visual-tool outputs (future observations) so downstream reasoning can start earlier.
Speculative planning: the agent pre-computes candidate action sequences based on predicted percepts, then verifies and corrects plans once real observations arrive.
Pipelined execution & rollback: run speculated plans in parallel with actual perception, validate results, and reconcile mismatches to preserve correctness while reducing end-to-end latency.
impact: Delivers lower latency and higher throughput for agentic multimodal systems, enabling more responsive, scalable, and cost-effective deployment of real-time vision+language agents.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline diagram: (a) traditional sequential agent loop vs (b) SpecEyes speculative pipelined loop highlighting overlap of perception, planning, and execution.
Timing diagram (Gantt-style): shows reduced agentic depth and end-to-end latency with speculation and the small rollback window.
Architecture block diagram: speculator, multimodal LLM, verifier/corrector, and tool interfaces with dataflow arrows.
Bar chart: empirical speedup (latency and throughput) and small accuracy trade-off (if any) to emphasize practical gains.
paper_title: SpecEyes: Accelerating Agentic Multimodal LLMs via Speculative Perception and Planning
paper_authors: Haoyu Huang, Jinfa Huang, Zhongwei Wan, Xiawu Zheng, Rongrong Ji
